name: r4-m04
statement: On MATH-500 at T 1.0, base + a(RL - base) behaves as a per-answer mixture of two whole endpoint modes: with probability p(a) an answer is drawn from RL's mode (boxed, long, RL-level 'Wait' rate, RL's per-problem accuracy) and otherwise from the a = 0 model's mode on the same prompt (plain base or cued base), so the share p(a) implied by accuracy, p = (score_a - score_0)/(score_RL - score_0) (0.76 plain and 0.66 cue at a = 0.25), is also the share recovered from 'Wait' rates, from answer format and from accuracy within the boxed answers.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math, theta(a) = base + a(RL - base) for 0 < a <= 1, MATH-500, one sample, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, plain and cue prompts. The a = 0 mode is the plain base (T3) for plain cells and the cued base (T1) for cue cells; the RL mode is RL plain (T2) or RL cue (rl_cue). Not covered: the harder 328 (where the mixture share from MATH-500 overpredicts, see conflicts), a > 1, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (n13 arms), Code-RL and other RL-Zero deltas, random-difference controls, Think-SFT.

imports.finding: Zero-RL multiplies an existing 'wait' marker that the Olmo-3 base already writes (4.94 per 1k) rather than creating it; RL-Zero-Math writes it far more often.
imports.how: The RL mode already exists in the base at low probability; the delta raises the probability of entering it, so 'Wait' rate is a per-answer mode marker rather than a quantity graded within each answer.

imports.finding: Scaling the rank-1 RL update by lambda from 0.1 to 1.0 raises MATH-500 quickly, then saturates.
imports.how: A fast-rising, saturating p(a) is what a switch probability gives: p(0.25) = 0.76 and p(0.5) = 0.92 in the plain row, then flat.

explains.how: With p(0.25) = 0.76 and p(0.5) = 0.92 the mixture score 224 + p(463 - 224) reproduces the plain row, and p saturates so the cue row is flat after 0.25.

explains.quote: Arms that recover accuracy also adopt RL's format and length
explains.how: Accuracy and format move together because both are properties of the same discrete RL mode that an answer either enters or not.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Same as above, independently recounted: an arm's accuracy tracks the share of its answers in RL's boxed, long mode.

explains.quote: D follows the answer format, not correctness
explains.how: The base-vs-RL difference is a format/mode choice, not a correctness signal, as expected if RL's effect is choosing which mode an answer is in.

explains.quote: theta0.5 fixes 53 and loses 11; RL plain fixes 65 and loses 12.
explains.how: At a = 0.5 most answers are already in RL's mode, so the fix/loss pattern is close to RL's own, with the shortfall from the remaining base-mode answers.

conflicts.how: With the MATH-500 cue shares (0.66, 0.89) the mixture predicts about 191 and 200 of 328 for theta 0.25 and 0.5 cue on the harder set; 182 and 190 were observed, so either p depends on problem difficulty or the mixture fails on long problems.

conflicts.quote: rl MATH-500 441/500 tokens 4036 | theta a 0.25, cue
conflicts.how: A 0.66 share of RL-mode answers (4,696 tokens) and 0.34 of cued-base answers (about 3,800-3,930) implies about 4,400 tokens per problem, more than the 4,036 observed (about 1.7 standard errors).
An orthogonal delta reaches the same gain with answers shorter than the base's, so the gain does not require RL's long mode; the mixture covers only the Math delta.

rival: The strongest rival is a graded intermediate policy: every theta answer shifts part of the way toward RL (somewhat more 'Wait', somewhat longer, more often boxed) and accuracy rises smoothly with a. Both fit the score rows. They come apart in the answers themselves. Under the mixture, the RL share estimated from 'Wait' rates (relative to RL's median), from the share of 'Answer:'-line answers, and from accuracy within boxed answers all equal the score-implied share (0.76 at plain a = 0.25), and boxed theta answers score like RL on those problems. Under the graded policy, theta 'Wait' rates bunch between the endpoints, so the Wait-based share falls well below 0.76, and the accuracy deficit spreads over boxed answers too (a boxed deficit near -0.10 instead of near -0.05).

predictions.experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base and RL plain endpoints
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T2 (RL plain) = s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl; T3 (base plain) = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. Use all rows of each file (500 each, cap hits included, no filtering; if a problem_index occurs twice keep the first row; missing rows are simply absent). For each row, rate = 1000 * (number of matches of the case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in the field text) / max(n_new, 1). Let m = median of the T2 rates (numpy.median). F_X = fraction of rows of file X with rate >= m (ties at m count as >=). Compute F_theta, F_T2, F_T3. Statistic S = (F_theta - F_T3) / (F_T2 - F_T3). Report S to 3 decimals.

predictions.experiment: Answer-format-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T3 = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included; first row per problem_index. A row is an 'answer-line' row if its text field contains no occurrence of the substring \boxed AND at least one line of the text, after stripping leading whitespace and any leading '*' or '#' characters, starts with the case-sensitive string 'Answer:'. s_X = (answer-line rows of X) / (rows of X). Statistic P = 1 - s_theta / s_T3. If s_T3 < 0.05 the statistic is undefined.
predictions.refuted_by: P below 0.60 or above 0.92, or undefined

predictions.experiment: Accuracy of theta0.25_plain boxed answers against RL plain on the same problems
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl (field score_v3); studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (field t2_right, grader v3, keyed by problem_index). Keep theta rows whose text contains the substring \boxed (cap hits included if they contain it; first row per problem_index). Drop rows whose problem_index has no entry in per_problem.json. For each kept row d = score_v3 (as 0/1; missing or null score_v3 counts as 0) - t2_right (as 0/1). Statistic D = mean of d over kept rows.

predictions.experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_cue against the cued base and RL cue endpoints
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl; RL cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl; T1 (base cue) = s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included, first row per problem_index. rate = 1000 * (matches of case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in text) / max(n_new, 1). m = numpy.median of the RL-cue rates. F_X = fraction of rows of X with rate >= m. S_cue = (F_theta - F_T1) / (F_RLcue - F_T1). If F_RLcue - F_T1 < 0.1 the statistic is undefined.
predictions.refuted_by: S_cue below 0.42 or above 0.92, or undefined

predictions.experiment: New cell: theta(0.125) = base + 0.125 (RL - base), stochastic bf16 rounding as in the existing theta cells, RL tokenizer, plain prompt, MATH-500 n = 500, one sample, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, seed base 74,000,000 + index, grader v3; report right of 500.
